findings.claim: The submodule bump changes the intelligence addon's process-wide logging configuration in addons/intelligence/app/main.py. It raises the `pdfminer` logger to ERROR, which is unrelated to Refine or alignment and is not in the touch-point list.
findings.impact: Every WARNING from pdfminer is now dropped for every PDF the addon extracts, not only the per-glyph FontBBox noise the comment names. If pdfminer reports a PDF problem only at WARNING level (degraded or partial text on a page that does not raise), it no longer appears in the addon log. This touches PDF extraction (the area of SPEC-ADDON-122), which this spec does not cover, and no invariant or test of this change looks at it.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/main.py:61-63 adds `logging.getLogger("pdfminer").setLevel(logging.ERROR)` straight after `logging.basicConfig`. The spec's Touch points list only aligner.py, refine.py, tests/, docs/addons/intelligence.md and the submodule pointer. No test in the change covers this line.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (reading only). Check: run PDF extraction on a PDF whose font lacks a FontBBox, or that makes pdfminer warn; before the bump the addon log shows pdfminer WARNING lines, after it shows none.

bucket_proposal.reason: It breaks no declared invariant (I1-I7 are about alignment and refine). It is an unplanned reach into logging and PDF extraction that the approved touch points do not cover.

findings.proposed_fix: Move the pdfminer log-level change into its own change with its own spec or touch point, or add main.py (logging) to this spec's touch points with a note on the scope.

findings.claim: The change edits the shared helper `extraction.store_original_if_absent` in addons/intelligence/app/extraction.py, adding a keyword-only `snapshot` parameter. This file and function are not in the touch-point list.
findings.impact: There is no behaviour change for the existing callers in routers/files.py:381 and :654, because they omit the argument and `snapshot or snapshot_transcript(...)` falls back as before. The kept-original API is shared by correction, redo and refine, though, and this reach into it is not recorded where the spec says the change goes. A non-empty `(str, str)` tuple is always truthy, so the `or` fallback cannot misfire for the refine caller.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/extraction.py:192-219 adds `snapshot: tuple[str, str] | None = None` and uses `row.chunks_json, row.words_json = snapshot or snapshot_transcript(session, file_id)`. The callers are refine.py:927 (new kwarg) and routers/files.py:381 and :654 (unchanged).

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is broken. I5 is served by this edit. The file is simply missing from the declared touch points.

findings.proposed_fix: Add `addons/intelligence/app/extraction.py: store_original_if_absent (optional pre-read snapshot)` to the touch points.

findings.claim: The change redefines the counts in the `intelligence.refine.completed` WebSocket event payload. `refined_count` now counts applied chunks, and `skipped_count` now includes chunks whose alignment failed. The touch-point list does not name this event, although the process asks touch points to list the events a change alters.
findings.impact: Anything that reads `refined_count` or `skipped_count` now sees different numbers for the same run. I found no consumer outside the addon's own tests (grep for refine.completed outside docs only hits refine.py and tests), so nothing a user can see changes. Spec §8 does describe the new meaning.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/workers/refine.py:872 no longer adds result.refined_count. Lines 948-949 add `len(applied_ids)` and `len(refined_window) - len(applied_ids)`. The payload is emitted at 1002-1014. docs/process/spec-and-design.md:41-43 says touch points include the 'endpoints and events it adds or changes'.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. tests/test_spec_addon_128_refine_alignment_failure.py asserts the new counts, for example refined_count 0 and skipped_count 3 in the failure cases.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is planned behaviour (spec §8), but the event is not listed as a touch point, and no invariant is broken.

findings.proposed_fix: Add `intelligence.refine.completed` (meaning of refined_count/skipped_count) to the touch points.

findings.claim: refine.py edits the module docstring and the `refine_chunks` docstring. These are prose in functions outside the listed refine.py touch points (`_run_refine_job`, `realign_words_for_chunk`, `rechunk_from_words`).
findings.impact: None for users. The new text matches the code: a window is applied only when the LLM answers for every chunk, and refine_chunks only mutates the in-memory snapshots. It would not lead a reader to a wrong code change.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/workers/refine.py module docstring (lines ~3-7) and the refine_chunks docstring (~145-151), per the diff hunks.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is a prose-only reach outside the listed functions, and no invariant is affected.

specification_compliance: Listed touch points that the diff reaches as planned: aligner._normalise_lang (ISO 639-2/3 table, `-`/`_` region split, lower-casing); refine._run_refine_job (per-chunk apply gated on realignment, kept original deferred to the first applied chunk with a snapshot taken before any write, generation bump and keyword reindex only when something was applied, one warning per run); realign_words_for_chunk (docstring only); rechunk_from_words (refined marks only on overlap with chunks refined before the rebuild); tests/; docs/addons/intelligence.md; the submodule pointer.

Places the diff reaches outside the declared touch points: addons/intelligence/app/main.py (pdfminer logging, TP-1); addons/intelligence/app/extraction.py store_original_if_absent (TP-2); the meaning of the intelligence.refine.completed event payload counts (TP-3); refine.py module and refine_chunks docstrings (TP-4).
Implicit touch points (docs/specs/refine-alignment-failure.md, docs/specs/INDEX.md, docs/process/reviews/...) are not reported.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The pdfminer logger is raised to ERROR process-wide (main.py:63). Nothing in the spec covers it.
_normalise_lang now also splits on `_`. Spec item 5 covers this, but every caller of the aligner is affected, including followup._realign_utterance through align_span (also stated in the spec).
regression_risks: PDF extraction warnings from pdfminer no longer reach the log, which can hide degraded PDF text reads (TP-1).

rechunk_from_words no longer marks rebuilt chunks as refined unless they overlap a chunk refined before the rebuild. Its only caller is _run_refine_job (refine.py:984), so this cannot reach other flows.
_load_words_in_range now runs twice per chunk with words (once in _run_refine_job, once inside realign_words_for_chunk). That costs performance only.
test_coverage: No test covers the main.py pdfminer log-level change.

extraction.store_original_if_absent with `snapshot` is exercised indirectly by the I5 tests (the kept original is the pre-run transcript even when the first chunk failed, and is written in the same transaction as the first applied chunk). The existing callers' default path is not re-tested by this change.
The new test suites for SPEC-ADDON-127 and 128 cover I1-I7 with a fake whisperx and run the real refine job against a temporary SQLite DB.
test_spec_addon_068 now stubs realign to 1 instead of 0, which keeps its chunks applied under the new rule. test_refine_speaker_id_clearing now expects refined_model None on rebuilt chunks.
